newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Corp to seek liquidation with Y274.5 bln debt.
newsitem.headline: All Corp to seek liquidation with Y274.5 bln debt.

text.p: Japanese non-bank financial institution All Corp announced on Thursday that it would seek court-protected special liquidation with total debts on borrowings worth 274.5 billion yen.
The special liquidation process would start in late March, it said in a statement.
The Tokyo-based non-bank said it had decided to hold a shareholders' meeting by the end of March in order to apply for court protection for special liquidation.
All Corp said that its cumulative debt exceeded its assets by 195.4 billion yen as of September 1996, and it would be hard to improve its business despite recent restructuring efforts.
The company was established in 1977 and engaged mainly in making loans, using real estate as collateral.

In the aftermath of the bursting of the late 1980s "bubble" of inflated asset prices, the company said it had suffered soaring non-performing loans and the situation had worsened due to sluggish real estate markets and bankruptcies by some of its borrowers.
All Corp also said that it would keep operating as a loan collecting company for a maximum of three years before completing its special liquidation process.
Trading in the company's shares, which are registered on the over-the-counter market, was suspended for Thursday's session ahead of the company's liquidation announcement.

The shares have been under surveillance -- a formal procedure in which dealing authorities signal caution about particular shares -- since mid-1995 because of the firm's deteriorating financial condition in the wake of the collapse of the 1980s "bubble" economy.
All Corp was in the business of making loans using real estate as collateral.

The bursting of the economic bubble and the subsequent slump in property values has induced a series of financial failures at Japanese non-banks, which are institutions which make loans but, unlike banks, cannot take deposits.

Japan suffered another major non-bank failure in October when Nichiei Finance filed for liquidation with debt liabilities of around one trillion yen. By one measure, this made Nichiei the largest such insolvency case in Japan in the post-war period.
